courses.title: Gospel Foundations
courses.description: Walk through the message of the Bible from creation to new life in Christ, reading the key passages for yourself.
objectives: Explain why people need salvation, using Scripture
Describe who Jesus is and what he did on the cross
Understand repentance and faith
Read and discuss key Gospel passages

lessons.title: God who made you
body: The Bible begins with God as Creator. People are made in his image and made to know him.
questions: What does it mean to be made in God's image?
According to Acts 17:27, how near is God?

lessons.title: What went wrong
body: Humanity turned away from God. The Bible calls this sin and describes its result as death.
questions: What changed after Genesis 3?
What two things are contrasted in Romans 6:23?

lessons.title: Who is Jesus?
body: The Gospels introduce Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God, who came to live among us.
questions: What did people say about Jesus in Mark 8?
Who do you say he is?

lessons.title: The cross and forgiveness
body: The New Testament teaches that Jesus died for sins and rose again, so people can be forgiven.
questions: How does Isaiah 53 describe the one who suffers?
What do we have in Christ, according to Colossians 1:14?

lessons.title: Repentance and faith
body: Jesus called people to repent and believe the good news. Salvation is received by faith as a gift.
questions: What two responses does Mark 1:15 call for?
Why is salvation called a gift?

lessons.title: A new life
body: Those who follow Jesus begin a new life, growing together with other believers.
questions: What does 'new creation' mean to you?
What next step will you take?

quiz.q: According to Romans 6:23, what is the gift of God?
options: Eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord
quiz.explain: Romans 6:23: "the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord."

quiz.q: Ephesians 2:8 says we are saved by grace through…
quiz.explain: Ephesians 2:8: "For by grace are ye saved through faith."

quiz.q: In John 3, who came to Jesus at night?
quiz.explain: John 3:1–2 tells of Nicodemus, a Pharisee, coming to Jesus by night.

quiz.q: Which two responses does Jesus call for in Mark 1:15?
quiz.explain: Mark 1:15: "repent ye, and believe the gospel."

quiz.q: 2 Corinthians 5:17 says that anyone in Christ is…
quiz.explain: 2 Corinthians 5:17: "if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature."

courses.title: First Steps of Discipleship
courses.description: Build the foundations of Christian life: assurance, the Word, prayer, fellowship, service and sharing your faith.
objectives: Understand the basis of assurance of salvation
Start daily habits of Bible reading and prayer
Belong to a fellowship
Take a first step in serving and sharing your faith

lessons.title: Assurance of Salvation
body: John wrote so that believers may know they have eternal life. Assurance rests on God's promise.
questions: Why did John write, according to 1 John 5:13?
What can separate us from God's love?

lessons.title: The Word of God
body: Disciples read, understand and obey God's word, which guides their lives.
questions: What does James 1:22 warn against?
What reading habit could you start this week?

lessons.title: Prayer
body: Prayer is talking with God. Jesus gave his disciples a pattern to follow.
questions: What does Philippians 4:6 say to do with worry?
Which line of the Lord's Prayer do you need most?

lessons.title: Fellowship
body: The first Christians devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread and prayer.
questions: What four things are listed in Acts 2:42?
Who could you encourage this week?

lessons.title: Serving Others
body: Jesus came to serve. His followers use their gifts to serve one another.
questions: What did Jesus come to do, according to Mark 10:45?
What gift could you use to serve?

lessons.title: Evangelism
body: Jesus sent his followers to make disciples of all nations, sharing the hope they have with gentleness.
questions: How should we answer according to 1 Peter 3:15?
Who in your life could you share with?

quiz.q: Acts 2:42 says the first believers devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and…
quiz.explain: Acts 2:42 lists "doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers."

quiz.q: Why did John write, according to 1 John 5:13?
options: So that you may know that you have eternal life
To describe the end of the world
quiz.explain: 1 John 5:13: "that ye may know that ye have eternal life."

quiz.q: James 1:22 says to be doers of the word, and not…
quiz.explain: James 1:22: "be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only."

quiz.q: According to Mark 10:45, the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to…
quiz.explain: Mark 10:45: "not to be ministered unto, but to minister."

quiz.q: In Matthew 28:19, what did Jesus send his disciples to do?
quiz.explain: Matthew 28:19: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations."

courses.title: Understanding the Heart
courses.description: Learn how thoughts and desires shape our choices, and how to build self-control, healthy relationships and a renewed mind.
objectives: Explain how thoughts influence the heart and actions
Recognize how temptation grows
Practice self-control and listening
Overcome isolation by building healthy relationships

lessons.title: The heart and its thoughts
body: The Bible treats the heart as the center of a person's thoughts, desires and choices. What happens in the heart shapes what we say and do.
questions: Why does Proverbs 4:23 say to guard the heart?
According to Mark 7:21–23, where do evil actions begin?

lessons.title: Where thoughts lead
body: James describes a chain: desire, then temptation, then sin. Genesis 3 shows how a single thought, accepted, changed Eve's view of what God had said.
questions: What are the steps in James 1:14–15?
What thought did Eve accept in Genesis 3?

lessons.title: Self-control
body: A person without self-control is compared to a city without walls. Self-control is listed as part of the fruit of the Spirit.
questions: What does a city without walls lack?
In which area of life do you most need self-control?

lessons.title: Renewing the mind
body: Paul calls believers to be transformed by the renewing of their minds, and to think about what is true, honest, just and pure.
questions: What does Romans 12:2 say not to be conformed to?
Which item in Philippians 4:8 do you want to think about more?

lessons.title: Overcoming isolation
body: Living far from home can be lonely. Scripture says two are better than one, because when one falls, the other can help them up.
questions: Who lifts you up when you fall?
Who could you encourage this week?

lessons.title: Listening and receiving advice
body: The wise listen to advice. James teaches us to be quick to hear, slow to speak and slow to anger.
questions: Why is it hard to accept advice?
Whose advice do you trust, and why?

quiz.q: Proverbs 4:23 says to keep your heart with all diligence, because…
options: out of it are the issues of life
no one else can see it
quiz.explain: Proverbs 4:23: "for out of it are the issues of life."

quiz.q: According to James 1:14, a person is tempted when…
options: they are drawn away of their own lust and enticed
quiz.explain: James 1:14: "every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed."

quiz.q: Proverbs 25:28 compares a person without rule over their own spirit to…
options: a city broken down, without walls
quiz.explain: Proverbs 25:28: "like a city that is broken down, and without walls."

quiz.q: Ecclesiastes 4:9–10 says two are better than one because…
options: if one falls, the other can lift him up
it is a law of nature
quiz.explain: Ecclesiastes 4:10: "if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow."

quiz.q: Romans 12:2 says to be transformed by…
quiz.explain: Romans 12:2: "be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind."

courses.title: Survival Korean 1
courses.description: Read Hangul and use the Korean you need for greetings, shopping, numbers and getting around.
objectives: Read Hangul syllable blocks
Greet people politely
Use both Korean number systems correctly
Ask for prices, items and directions

lessons.title: Meet Hangul
body: Hangul is the Korean alphabet, created in the 15th century under King Sejong. It has 14 basic consonants and 10 basic vowels.
Letters are written together in syllable blocks. For example, 한 is made of ㅎ (h) + ㅏ (a) + ㄴ (n).
Practice: 안녕하세요 is five blocks: 안 + 녕 + 하 + 세 + 요. Try reading it slowly, one block at a time.

lessons.title: Reading syllable blocks
body: A block starts with a consonant, followed by a vowel: 가 (ga), 나 (na), 다 (da). Some blocks add a final consonant underneath: 각 (gak), 산 (san).
When a syllable starts with a vowel sound, the silent consonant ㅇ holds the first place: 아 (a), 오 (o), 우 (u).
Practice: read 가 나 다 라 마 바 사 아 자 차 카 타 파 하.

lessons.title: Greetings and polite speech
body: Korean changes its endings to show politeness. The everyday polite ending is -요: 괜찮아요 (it's okay), 좋아요 (it's good).
The formal ending -습니다 / -ㅂ니다 is used at work, in announcements and with people you should show respect to: 감사합니다 (thank you).
Useful greetings: 안녕하세요 (hello), 감사합니다 (thank you), 죄송합니다 (I'm sorry), 수고하셨습니다 (thank you for your hard work, said after work).

lessons.title: At the store
body: 이거 얼마예요? How much is this?
이거 주세요. Please give me this one.
카드 돼요? Can I pay by card?
봉투 주세요. A bag, please.

lessons.title: Two number systems
body: Korean uses two sets of numbers. Sino-Korean numbers are used for money, dates, phone numbers and minutes: 일 (1), 이 (2), 삼 (3), 사 (4), 오 (5), 육 (6), 칠 (7), 팔 (8), 구 (9), 십 (10).
Native Korean numbers are used for counting things, age and hours on the clock: 하나 (1), 둘 (2), 셋 (3), 넷 (4), 다섯 (5), 여섯 (6), 일곱 (7), 여덟 (8), 아홉 (9), 열 (10).
Example: 오천 원 is 5,000 won (Sino-Korean).

lessons.title: Getting around
body: 지하철역이 어디예요? Where is the subway station?
화장실이 어디예요? Where is the restroom?
(place)까지 가 주세요. Please take me to (place). Useful in a taxi.
여기서 내려요. I'm getting off here.

quiz.q: How many basic consonants does Hangul have?
quiz.explain: Hangul has 14 basic consonants and 10 basic vowels.

quiz.q: Which number system is used for prices, like 5,000 won?
quiz.explain: Money uses Sino-Korean numbers: 오천 원.

quiz.q: What does 이거 주세요 mean?
quiz.explain: 이거 주세요 means "Please give me this one."

quiz.q: Which ending makes everyday speech polite?
quiz.explain: -요 is the everyday polite ending, as in 괜찮아요.

quiz.q: Which consonant is silent at the start of a syllable?
quiz.explain: ㅇ is silent at the start of a syllable, as in 아.

courses.title: Settling in Korea
courses.description: The essentials for your first months in Korea: documents, transport, healthcare, daily routines and where to get help.
objectives: Know the residence card and visa basics
Get around with public transport
Use the healthcare system
Know who to call for help

lessons.title: Your residence card
body: If you will stay in Korea for more than 90 days, you must register as a foreign resident within 90 days of entering Korea. You'll receive a residence card.
Book an appointment at your local immigration office through Hi Korea (hikorea.go.kr). Carry your card with you, and report your new address when you move, within the legal deadline.
Rules change. Always check Hi Korea or call 1345 for your own situation.

lessons.title: Your visa and your stay
body: Your visa type decides what activities you may do in Korea, such as study or a specific kind of work.
Apply for an extension or change before your permitted stay ends. Late applications, or working outside what your visa allows, can lead to fines or other penalties.
For advice on your own case, ask the Immigration Contact Center (1345) or a qualified professional.

lessons.title: Getting around
body: Buy a T-money card at a convenience store or subway station and top it up with cash. It works on buses, subways and many taxis.
Naver Map and KakaoMap give the most reliable directions in Korea.
Tap your card when getting on and off buses to receive transfer discounts.

lessons.title: Staying healthy
body: Many foreign residents who stay six months or more are enrolled in National Health Insurance. Check your status at nhis.or.kr.
Visit a local clinic (의원) for everyday illness and bring your residence card. Pharmacies (약국) fill prescriptions.
In an emergency, call 119.

lessons.title: Trash and recycling
body: Household trash goes in volume-based trash bags (종량제 봉투), sold at convenience stores.
Food waste and recyclables are separated. Rules differ by district, so ask your neighbors or building manager.

lessons.title: Getting help
body: 112: police. 119: fire and ambulance. 109: suicide prevention counseling.
1345: Immigration Contact Center (multilingual). 1577-1366: Danuri helpline for multicultural families.
You're not alone. The DHL community and mentors are here to help.

quiz.q: What number do you call for fire and ambulance in Korea?
quiz.explain: 119 is for fire and ambulance; 112 is for police.

quiz.q: Which number is the multilingual Immigration Contact Center?
quiz.explain: 1345 is the Immigration Contact Center.

quiz.q: What is the common transit card in Korea called?
quiz.explain: T-money works on buses, subways and many taxis.

quiz.q: Which map apps give the most reliable directions in Korea?
quiz.explain: Naver Map and KakaoMap are the most reliable in Korea.

quiz.q: Where does household trash go?
quiz.explain: Household trash goes in volume-based trash bags sold at convenience stores.

courses.title: Servant Leadership Basics
courses.description: Learn to lead the way Jesus did: character first, serving others, mentoring and handling conflict.
objectives: Describe servant leadership from Scripture
Understand the character a leader needs
Begin mentoring one person
Handle conflict biblically

lessons.title: Servant Leadership
body: Jesus defined greatness as serving. Leaders go first in humility.
Practical assignment: Serve someone in your group this week without being asked, then reflect on what you learned.

lessons.title: Biblical Leadership
body: Character before skill: what Scripture asks of those who lead God's people.
Practical assignment: Read 1 Timothy 3 with a mentor and choose one area of character to work on.

lessons.title: Paul's Leadership
body: How Paul trained others, entrusted responsibility and kept going through hardship.
Practical assignment: Map Paul's 2 Timothy 2:2 chain onto your own life: who taught you, and whom will you teach?

lessons.title: Mentoring
body: Walking with one person over time, the heart of multiplication.
Practical assignment: Meet with one younger believer three times this month.

lessons.title: Small Group Leadership
body: Planning a meeting, asking good questions and caring for members.
Practical assignment: Co-lead one small group session with an experienced leader.

lessons.title: Conflict Management
body: Handling disagreement biblically, quickly and with grace.
Practical assignment: Study Matthew 18:15–17 and role-play a difficult conversation with your mentor.

quiz.q: In Mark 10:43, what must a person be to be great among Jesus' followers?
quiz.explain: Mark 10:43: "whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister."

quiz.q: In 2 Timothy 2:2, what should faithful people be able to do?
quiz.explain: 2 Timothy 2:2: "faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also."

quiz.q: According to Matthew 18:15, what is the first step when someone sins against you?
options: Go and tell him his fault between you and him alone
quiz.explain: Matthew 18:15 begins with a private conversation.

quiz.q: What is DHL's core leadership question?
options: How many people follow this person?
Can this person now help another person grow?
How long has this person been a Christian?
Can this person speak in public?
quiz.explain: DHL measures leadership by whether someone can help another person grow.

quiz.q: 1 Timothy 3:1–7 focuses mostly on a leader's…
quiz.explain: Most of the qualities listed are about character and conduct.

courses.title: Online Ministry Host
courses.description: Serve by creating content, hosting online Bible studies and building safe online communities that lead to real relationships.
objectives: Plan content with a clear next step
Host a welcoming online Bible study
Moderate a safe group chat
Move people from online to real-life community

lessons.title: Creating Christian content
body: Plan posts that serve a real need, point to Jesus and invite a next step.
Tip: Every post should answer: what do I want someone to do after seeing this?

lessons.title: Social media evangelism
body: Move from comments to conversations to invitations, respectfully.
Tip: Reply to every sincere comment, and invite people to the community, not just to 'like'.

lessons.title: Online Bible study
body: Run a simple, repeatable online study that people can join from anywhere in Korea.
Tip: Send the passage the day before so people can read ahead.

lessons.title: Zoom ministry
body: Host warm online meetings: welcome people, use breakout rooms and follow up.
Tip: Have a co-host who greets newcomers by name in the chat.

lessons.title: Digital community building
body: Build group chats that feel safe, friendly and purposeful.
Tip: Write simple group rules and appoint two moderators.

lessons.title: Online discipleship
body: Walk with someone one-to-one using messages, calls and shared reading plans.
Tip: Online is the bridge: plan an in-person meeting as soon as you can.

quiz.q: Every post should answer which question?
options: How many likes will this get?
What do I want someone to do after seeing this?
quiz.explain: Each post should lead to a clear next step.

quiz.q: When should you send the passage for an online Bible study?
quiz.explain: Sending it the day before lets people read ahead.

quiz.q: What is the co-host's key job in a Zoom meeting?
quiz.explain: A co-host who welcomes newcomers makes people feel they belong.

quiz.q: What helps a group chat stay safe and welcoming?
options: Adding as many people as possible
quiz.explain: Simple rules and two moderators keep a group healthy.

quiz.q: Complete the DHL principle: "Online is not the destination. Online is the…"
quiz.explain: Online is the bridge to real relationships.
